C-DEV-ENV-ISOLATION.Summary: Give ordinary development runs their own profile namespace by default, make the dev-smoke cycle kill only the processes it spawned and report a busy dev port honestly instead of killing blindly, and document the security gate's POSIX-only review-lane lock together with the Windows-candidate handoff — so local verification can no longer mutate production profile state or touch processes it does not own.
C-DEV-ENV-ISOLATION.Problem: Confirmed against the current read-only state of the the 2026-11-21 mainline inspection tree. Profile share (audit ai-readiness 2026-11-20, group score 65): the compiled configuration carries the production identifier `com.xronocode.mark` (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:5), and main.rs binds exactly that identifier once before any state access — `mt_paths::initialize_application_identifier(&context.config().identifier)` (src-tauri/src/main.rs:296-300) — after which mt_paths derives the OS cache and durable roots per identifier (src-tauri/src/mt_paths.rs:96-131 and 139-173; canonical constant mt_paths.rs:29). The namespace split machinery already works for isolated acceptance builds, which merge a distinct identifier into the Tauri config (`com.xronocode.mark.test.<slug>.<sha>` in tools/build-test-artifact.mjs:171-176, `com.xronocode.mark.qa.…` in tools/prepare-qa-artifacts.mjs:92,133). The ordinary dev paths have no such merge: `npm run tauri:dev` (package.json:14) and the dev-smoke cycle (`dev:smoke`/`dev:quick`/`dev:check`, package.json:35-37) build and launch a binary that binds the production identifier, so a dev session reads and writes the real user profile — preferences and the persisted session profile under cache_root/preferences.json (src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs:103), crash logs under cache_root (src-tauri/src/m001_panic.rs:58), security bookmarks under data_root (src-tauri/src/m047_bookmarks.rs:67), extension discovery and the live endpoint under data_root (src-tauri/src/m045_ext/discovery.rs:44-46, src-tauri/src/m045_ext/live_endpoint.rs:63), rollback staging (src-tauri/src/m068_rollback.rs:102,393), keyring credentials whose service name is the same identifier (src-tauri/src/m019_datacenter.rs:22, src-tauri/src/m045_ext/auth.rs:82) and default-handler targeting (src-tauri/src/m021_default_handler.rs:349). Process interference (audit F-001): tools/dev-smoke.sh checks the fixed shared address http://localhost:1420 (dev-smoke.sh:16) and accepts any HTTP 200 as "dev server already running" (dev-smoke.sh:52-58), adopting a foreign server from another working copy as its own result; on restart it kills by broad cmdline patterns — `pkill -f "vite.*serve"`, `pkill -f "npm run dev"` (dev-smoke.sh:46-50), `pkill -f "target/debug/mark"` (dev-smoke.sh:41-44) — so a busy port or a stale-looking process list is answered by killing processes this check never spawned, in any repository on the host; no owned-PID record exists anywhere in the script (the only PID it captures is a local `$!` in launch_mark, dev-smoke.sh:73-74). Audit anchors: tools/dev-smoke.sh:13-17, 41-62, 71-88. Gate portability (audit F-002): the mandatory pre-commit/pre-push review in tools/security_gate.py imports fcntl and takes the POSIX flock lane before any candidate work — `import fcntl` at tools/security_gate.py:1269 and the `lane()` context manager with `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` at :1271-1283, wrapped around candidate construction, deterministic scan and model review in `review()` at :1266-1291 and :1289-1319 — so on stock Windows Python the gate fails at the module import with no documented way out; CONTRIBUTING.md:70 defers entirely to docs/commit-push-safety.md, whose model-review section (:49-75) states the Windows machine is "required only for Windows-version testing, which is outside this gate" but never names the gate's supported hosts nor a handoff that preserves candidate identity and receipt for a Windows-authored candidate.
C-DEV-ENV-ISOLATION.Relationship: Builds directly on C-STABILIZE-PROFILE-ISOLATION (configured immutable namespace binding in M-022, initialized from the generated Tauri Context in M-001 before any state access) and C-STABILIZE-NATIVE-PROFILE-CLOSEOUT (native credential, discovery and default-handler consumers already route the configured identifier in M-019/M-021/M-045) — both landed, so this change only defaults the dev lane onto the existing split instead of adding split machinery. The QA/acceptance isolated-build pipeline (tools/build-test-artifact.mjs, tools/prepare-qa-artifacts.mjs) is the identifier-merge precedent this change extends to plain dev runs; the owned-PID quit discipline precedent lives in tools/qa-artifact-smoke.mjs (processQuery matching bundle path, identifier and owned PID list before any quit, :39-71) under C-QA-MACOS-LAUNCH-GATE, which stays unchanged. The security-gate item is documentation plus a contract-accuracy note only: the lane-lock design is owned by C-SAFETY-REVIEW-LANES/C-SAFETY-LOCAL-FIRST-REVIEW lineage and is not redesigned here. Independent of C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY (session-profile write durability — orthogonal transport fix on the same M-005 store). Tasking source: the ai-readiness audit report (2026-11-20) — F-001 (local launch verification touches neighboring processes) and F-002 (no documented way to complete the mandatory review for a Windows candidate), including the audit's own recommendation to bind server, logs, profile and process termination to the current run and to align the separate-profile use with the existing acceptance procedure. Delivered through the repository technical-debt lane; lane departure, train accounting and release remain separate owner-controlled steps.

Goals.Goal: Dev runs default to a separate profile namespace through the existing mt_paths split: a debug-build dev default identifier (proposed `com.xronocode.mark.dev`, final value confirmed by the plan) is bound at the same boot point that binds the configured identifier today (main.rs, before rollback, reconciliation, panic logging or preferences access), so every ordinary dev path — `npm run tauri:dev` and the dev-smoke build/launch cycle alike — resolves all audited stores under the dev root: preferences and persisted session profile (M-005), crash logs (M-001), security bookmarks (M-047), extension discovery, live endpoint and extension credentials (M-045), datacenter credentials (M-019), default-handler targeting (M-021), rollback staging (M-068). Release binaries bind exactly the configured Context identifier; canonical release paths stay byte-identical. An explicit, documented escape hatch (debug builds only, non-default) lets a developer deliberately bind the production namespace from a dev build for migration testing.

dev-smoke kills only PIDs it spawned: the cycle records the PIDs it launches (dev server and mark binary) in a run-scoped pidfile, restart and cleanup paths kill only recorded, still-owned PIDs, and a busy dev port produces an honest report naming the owner (PID and command) with the run failing — never a blind pattern kill and never adopting a foreign HTTP 200 as readiness for this build.

The security gate's POSIX-only lock assumption is documented as the Windows handoff: CONTRIBUTING.md names the supported hosts for the mandatory review (POSIX flock lanes) and docs/commit-push-safety.md describes how a Windows-authored candidate is carried to a supported review host preserving its exact candidate identity and receipt; tools/security_gate.py's module contract records the POSIX-only dependency. No Windows lock implementation.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact ObservedWriteScope, enumerated by reading the current tree:

Planned new files beyond the observed set: tests/tools/dev-smoke.test.mjs (fixture-based pins for the kill and busy-port paths). No other new files; no new dependencies (the port-owner report uses host tools already present on supported dev hosts: lsof/ps on macOS and Linux). tools/security_gate.py is touched only in its module contract text (DEPENDS/SCOPE note naming the POSIX-only lane lock); its behavior, command surface and receipts are unchanged, and tests/security/test_security_gate.py stays green without edits.

No change to production identifier behavior: release builds bind exactly the Context-configured identifier (the dev default and the escape-hatch env override are compiled or gated so release binaries ignore them); the canonical release identifier, version, bundle identity, updater and profile migration behavior are unchanged; C-STABILIZE-PROFILE-ISOLATION's binding order is preserved — CLI help/version exit without profile access and the namespace is bound before rollback, reconciliation, panic logging or preferences access.

The escape hatch is documentation-first and fail-safe by default: the production-namespace binding from a dev build happens only via the explicit documented override, never silently; the doc states its purpose (migration testing) and its risk honestly.

dev-smoke stays a local POSIX dev tool: owned-PID tracking replaces the pkill -f patterns; a foreign-port report names the owner process and refuses to proceed; --check mode keeps reporting health without killing anything; the BLOCK-marker launch verification and MARK_SKIP_MIGRATION usage keep their current semantics unless the plan explicitly re-pins them.

Repository artifacts stay English and the GRACE surface stays synchronized (module contracts, module maps, graph and verification entries for M-001, M-022 and M-064); no version change, release, publication or deploy is authorized by this specification.

Baseline divergence: this draft was written against the 2026-11-21 mainline inspection tree; the plan must bind to the actual prepared delivery baseline and rerun the pinned suites on that baseline. Approval of this specification alone does not approve an unwritten plan, apply/archive, lane departure or release.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No containerization: no Docker/VM/sandbox wrapper around dev runs, no per-worktree port allocation service — the dev namespace and pidfile split solve the audited hazards without new infrastructure.
No full multi-tenant profile support (multiple simultaneously isolated user profiles inside the product) — recorded as a separate backlog item, not this change.
No Windows implementation of the review lock: no Win32 LockFile port, no pure-Python lock alternative, no gate behavior change on any host — the Windows item is documentation and handoff only.

No change to the QA/acceptance isolated-build pipeline (tools/build-test-artifact.mjs, tools/prepare-qa-artifacts.mjs, tools/qa-launch-gate.mjs, tools/qa-artifact-smoke.mjs keep their own namespace, gate and owned-PID machinery), no profile migration, no credential-store policy change.
No redesign of the security gate's review lanes, executor resolution, override receipt or scan-diff mode; only the contract note and the host/handoff documentation move.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first unit pin in src-tauri/src/mt_paths.rs: dev_namespace_default_resolves_disjoint_roots — with a synthetic environment lookup, the dev default identifier resolves cache and data roots that are disjoint from the release roots and carry the dev identifier, extending the existing configured_identifiers_have_disjoint_cache_and_data_roots family; a paired pin proves release binding is byte-identical to the current canonical paths (canonical_identifier_preserves_existing_cache_and_data_roots stays green unchanged) and that the escape-hatch override is honored in debug builds and absent in release builds.

Failing-first fixture-based pins in the new tests/tools/dev-smoke.test.mjs, driving tools/dev-smoke.sh with a sandbox HOME and PATH-shimmed process tools: refuses_foreign_pids — a foreign process matching the old patterns is not killed when it is absent from the run's pidfile; busy_port_reports_owner_and_does_not_kill — a foreign listener on the dev port produces the honest ownership report (PID and command) and the run fails without any kill; kills_only_spawned_pids — the restart and cleanup paths kill exactly the pidfile-recorded PIDs and nothing else; adopts_no_foreign_200 — a 200 from an untracked port owner is not reported as this build's ready server.

Existing suites stay green without weakened assertions: the full mt_paths test module, the boot-order pins protecting C-STABILIZE-PROFILE-ISOLATION's binding order, and tests/security/test_security_gate.py (the gate contract note moves no behavior).

Documentation requirements are met and reviewed: CONTRIBUTING.md names the supported hosts for the mandatory pre-commit/pre-push review; docs/commit-push-safety.md carries the Windows-candidate handoff (supported review host, exact candidate identity and receipt carried across); the dev-profile default and the migration-testing escape hatch are documented where dev workflow is described; tools/security_gate.py's contract records the POSIX-only lane lock.

Graph ownership, module contracts, module maps and verification entries describe the final implementation: M-022 (dev namespace default and validation), M-001 (boot binding with the debug-gated default and override) and M-064 (contract DEPENDS note) are synchronized with their V- entries before delivery is called integrated.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: New Rust pins: the dev namespace resolves disjoint roots from release under synthetic environments; release binding stays byte-identical and the escape hatch is debug-only. Failing-first proof must detect the current hazards: a dev build binding the production identifier, the pattern-based kill of untracked processes, and the silent adoption of a foreign port-1420 answer. Existing mt_paths and gate suites pass unchanged.

New fixture pins: dev-smoke refuses foreign PIDs, reports the busy-port owner without killing, kills only pidfile-recorded PIDs, and never counts a foreign 200 as readiness. The real two-working-copies concurrency check from the audit (launch in one worktree leaves the other worktree's processes, logs and profile untouched) remains a hosted/manual acceptance step and is not substituted by a shim.

Documentation evidence: the supported-host note and the Windows handoff are present in CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/commit-push-safety.md, preserving candidate identity and receipt semantics as pinned by the gate suite. Before archiving: grace lint --path . --change C-DEV-ENV-ISOLATION --assertions final --run-commands, then grace lint --path . --assertions current and grace status --path . --with modules --json.

Assumptions.Assumption: The dev namespace value `com.xronocode.mark.dev` is an agent proposal consistent with the existing `com.xronocode.mark.test.*` and `com.xronocode.mark.qa.*` patterns and valid under mt_paths' identifier validator (alnum/dash/underscore dot-parts); the plan records the owner's confirmation or adjustment before implementation.

The dev default lever is a debug-build (debug_assertions-gated) binding with an explicit environment override for migration testing, so both the tauri:dev path and the dev-smoke cargo-built binary are covered by one mechanism and release binaries need no guard; the plan may instead choose a Tauri dev-config merge for the tauri:dev path only if it still covers the dev-smoke binary, and the exact override name follows the MARK_SKIP_MIGRATION env precedent (proposal: MARK_PROFILE_IDENTIFIER) with the owner confirming the final name.

The brief's wording "dev-smoke kills PIDs by port (busy-port = kill, not report)" is mapped to the observed mechanism: the current script has no lsof-by-port kill in any inspected copy; the audited hazards are the fixed shared port 1420 whose HTTP 200 is adopted blindly (dev-smoke.sh:52-58) and the broad pkill -f pattern kills (dev-smoke.sh:41-50) that fire on the restart path when the port is not healthy. The spec words the Problem and the busy-port goal by the observed mechanism; the port-owner report introduces lsof/ps-based ownership reporting on the supported dev hosts.

mark-safety/gate.py was not found under owner-local skills; the audited gate is the repository's tools/security_gate.py (M-064, tests/security/test_security_gate.py). The fcntl reference named by the audit is the function-scoped import and flock lane in review() (tools/security_gate.py:1266-1291), taken before any candidate check, so stock Windows Python fails at the first review invocation.
